title: Stake architecture
canonical_definition: Reuse canonical $420 custody/accounting. Do not create an unrelated collateral treasury.

parent_requirement.title: ComputeStake
parent_requirement.purpose: Provide worker/verifier collateral and objective economic consequences without conflating Compute custody with validator stake or payer escrow.

authority: read worker collateral position state for admission

canonical_custody_model.rule: Compute collateral uses a dedicated registered VAULT_COLLATERAL instance inside the canonical 420Vault family. A distinct Vault instance isolates collateral liabilities from payer escrow, but it is not a second treasury or accounting system.
canonical_custody_model.backing_rule: Every active/slashable position amount must be backed by canonical Vault balance/accounting and a uniquely bound collateral obligation; internal mappings alone are never custody.
canonical_custody_model.solvency_rule: Aggregate active, exiting, slashable, claimable and released collateral accounting must never exceed the corresponding canonical Vault backing.
canonical_custody_model.authorization_rule: A future ComputeStake controller may receive only narrowly scoped collateral-vault actions required for stake lifecycle, exit, objective slash reallocation and reward accounting; no arbitrary withdraw, beneficiary redirection, generic transfer, treasury budget or payer-escrow authority.
canonical_custody_model.isolation_rule: Worker/verifier positions and policy revisions use unique domain-separated position identities; one position cannot consume or slash another participant's backing.

non_substitutes: validator bond state exposed by Stake420/ValidatorRegistry
verification verdict without independently qualified final slash authorization

lifecycle_architecture.stake: payer/participant-origin native $420 enters the registered collateral Vault atomically with creation/increase of the exact position-backed obligation; successful return requires backing/accounting parity.
lifecycle_architecture.request_exit: marks the canonical ComputeStake position exiting and freezes the applicable withdrawal delay while collateral remains backed and slashable according to the bound policy.
lifecycle_architecture.unstake: may release only matured, non-forfeited collateral to the immutable position owner/beneficiary after delay and all policy/dispute locks; no admin-recipient substitution.
lifecycle_architecture.slash: may consume only objectively proven, final, policy-bound slashable collateral for the exact subject/position/policy revision; allegation or nonfinal review is insufficient.
lifecycle_architecture.reward: records/credits only an authorized reward source and may not mint, seize payer escrow, or fabricate Vault backing.
lifecycle_architecture.historical_reads: later policy/source/identity changes cannot rewrite historical position revisions, stake references, slash evidence or already-final entitlements.

authority_boundaries: ComputeStake lifecycle authority does not imply validator lifecycle, consensus, Civic governance, Treasury, bridge, arbitrary-wallet or payer-escrow authority.
420Vault remains custody/release authority; ComputeStake owns collateral lifecycle semantics and bounded instructions only.
ComputeEscrow payer obligations and ComputeStake collateral obligations remain separately backed, separately identified and never netted or silently reclassified.
Worker/verifier registration or reputation does not create stake.
A verifier verdict/challenge record is evidence input only; CMP-1.5.5 must establish objective slash authorization and finality.
Emergency/governance suspension may stop unsafe new activity but cannot redirect collateral, fabricate slash evidence or confiscate matured valid entitlement.
Validator Stake420/ValidatorRegistry collateral is a distinct consensus-economic domain and cannot satisfy IComputeStakeSource420.
deliberately_deferred: worker stake mutation and custody operations

deployment_state.note: CMP-1.5.0 is an architecture freeze only.
